prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is a general, ligand-controlled method that turned a difficult bond construction into routine practice in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. The catalytic cycles were established mechanistically, and the work has been independently reproduced for about three decades. My opening ranked my own field, molecular sieves (B046), first, but B046 has no support from any colleague and its five-name attribution is diffuse and partly entangled with industrial work. B060 is the candidate in my ranking with both scientific strength and a clean, defensible allocation. Buchwald and Hartwig independently built the practical catalyst systems. Dropping Kosugi, whom I included as a third name in the opening, gives the fairer and more conventional two-person set. The 2010 prize covered C-C coupling only, so this is a distinct and overdue recognition rather than a repeat.
statement.case_against: The 2010 cross-coupling prize may make the committee feel the area is already honored, and C-N coupling can be read as an extension of the same palladium paradigm rather than a new principle. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work and the independent Buchwald and Hartwig lines raise real priority questions. Next to targeted protein degradation (B026), which opens a new pharmacological modality and has the broadest first-place support, B060 may look conservative.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B060 first because bulky, electron-rich ligand design made C-N coupling general and predictable, the 2010 prize covered only C-C coupling, and Buchwald and Hartwig form a clean two-person configuration with Kosugi as a precursor.
responses.response: I agree with the scientific case and now drop Kosugi from my own proposal, as the precedent was not a general catalytic method. I would add one condition to the citation. It should say carbon-nitrogen coupling explicitly, so the 2010 overlap argument is answered in the text. Hartwig's mechanistic work on oxidative addition and reductive elimination is where our structural evidence is strongest. That is the evidence I would use to rebut any claim that the area is already covered.

responses.point: Aili ranks B026 first as a genuine new modality in which chemically induced proximity degrades rather than inhibits a target, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as the conceptual core and Ciulli as a contested fourth.
responses.response: I accept that PROTACs and molecular glues are conceptually the more novel advance, and I placed them lower only on maturity, not on originality. As far as I know no PROTAC drug is approved. Handa's cereblon work is well established, but the structural evidence for ternary-complex geometry, where Ciulli's crystallography is strongest, has been decisive for rational design. Deshaies' PROTAC role is real, but the committee should test whether Ciulli deserves a place before settling on the trio, because that choice changes the citation from a concept to a mechanism-based design principle. I would keep B026 as a strong alternative and revisit it once the maturity picture is clearer.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks Gray and Winkler's long-range electron transfer first and nitrogenase second, valuing mechanisms stated in physical terms and tested by kinetics, while noting that nitrogenase mechanism is not fully settled.
responses.response: I agree on nitrogenase. The FeMo-cofactor structure with its carbide is well established, but the E4 state and the N2 binding site are still debated, so a mechanism prize would be premature. A structure-only prize would also leave out the part colleagues want to recognize. That is why I rank it third rather than first. On B028 I respect the physical clarity, but with Marcus theory already honored and credit shared with Dutton, Moser and others, I cannot judge from the opening files that a two-person Gray and Winkler attribution is safe.

responses.point: Linke ranks sequencing by synthesis first as a chemistry-driven invention with enormous impact, and Balasubramanian and Klenerman as the Solexa core, while noting that Rothberg, Mayer and Ju complicate credit.
responses.response: The scale of impact is not in doubt, but I am less convinced than Linke that this is the strongest chemistry case. The platform lineages (Solexa, 454, nanopore and others) are separate achievements, and a prize limited to Solexa leaves out much of how massively parallel sequencing came about. I also share Aqvist's concern that the field overlaps with Sanger and with Physiology or Medicine. Compared with C-N coupling, where the attribution is clean, B067 leaves a larger unresolved allocation question.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat C-N coupling as a distinct achievement or as covered by the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Whether Kosugi's precursor work warrants any credit, which I now doubt.
Whether protein degradation is mature enough without an approved PROTAC drug, and whether Ciulli rather than Deshaies or Handa belongs in the trio.
I have not seen the other members' views beyond the opening ballots, so I do not know whether support for B060 extends beyond Somfai and me.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict specific to B060 is apparent from my profile. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which is not relevant to these candidates. I have a broad network in porous materials and electron crystallography that includes some credited people in B046 and B068. I would recuse myself from any vote that depends on my own field's candidates, as a precaution, but this does not affect my B060 preference.
